the method proposed in this thesis is a promising approach for personalized coronary hemodynamic simulations.

The main takeaway from our work is that

a personalized CFD model of the coronary tree can be constructed from non-invasivly acquired patient data at the rest state, and the boundary conditions at hyperemic flow can be derived using a transfer function model of the vasodilation process.
the estimation of hyperemic resistances from the rest state is a crucial step for obtaining accurate simulations under hyperemic conditions.

the proposed method can be used to personalize the coronary hemodynamic simulations for a patient, which in turn can be utilized in the clinical practice for the diagnosis of coronary artery diseases.
